title: Find the Celebrity in One Pass
statement:
In a group of `n` people labelled `0` to `n - 1`, a **celebrity** is a person who knows nobody else in the group, while every other person in the group knows them.

You are given an `n × n` matrix `knows`, where `knows[i][j] = 1` means person `i` knows person `j` and `0` means they do not. Knowing is not necessarily symmetric, and `knows[i][i] = 0` for every `i`.

Print the label of the celebrity, or `-1` if the group has no celebrity. A group can have at most one celebrity.

**Follow-up:** in a real system the matrix is too large to scan, so find the answer by looking at only `O(n)` entries of it (a single pass to narrow down to one candidate, then a verification pass) instead of examining all `n²` entries.
input_format:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains `n` integers (`0` or `1`): row `i` of the matrix `knows`.
output_format: Print a single integer: the label of the celebrity, or `-1` if there is none.

examples.explanation: Person 1 knows nobody (row 1 is all zeros), and persons 0 and 2 both know person 1 (column 1 holds a 1 in rows 0 and 2). So person 1 is the celebrity.
Everybody knows exactly one other person, so nobody satisfies 'knows nobody'. There is no celebrity.
Person 0 knows nobody, and persons 1, 2 and 3 all know person 0. The other rows contain 1s, so none of them can be the celebrity.

complexity.time: O(n) matrix lookups (plus O(n²) just to read the input)

hints: If person a knows person b, then a cannot be the celebrity. If a does not know b, then b cannot be the celebrity. So one lookup always eliminates one of the two people.
Keep a running candidate and compare it against each next person; after one pass only a single candidate survives.
The survivor is only a candidate: verify that its row has no 1s (outside itself) and that its column has 1s everywhere else.
